summary: Set up centralized log forwarding: node2 runs an inventory systemd service (logging heartbeats via logger -t inventory) forwarded by rsyslog over TCP/514 to node1, where rsyslog (imtcp) writes matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Config is persisted via systemd enablement and rsyslog.d files, and firewalld on node1 permanently allows tcp/514. Verified the pipeline survives independent reboots of both node1 and node2, with boot-id proof of actual restarts and continuous, correctly-timestamped log delivery afterward.
actions_performed: Surveyed both RHEL7 nodes: confirmed rsyslog 8.24.0 installed on both, no pre-existing inventory app, sudo available, firewalld active on node1.
Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh and systemd unit inventory.service on node2 that emits periodic heartbeat log lines tagged 'inventory' via logger; enabled and started it.

Added /etc/rsyslog.d/inventory-forward.conf on node2 forwarding programname=='inventory' messages via TCP (@@) to node1 with a disk-assured action queue (infinite retry, save-on-shutdown) for resilience during node1 downtime.

Added /etc/rsyslog.d/inventory-receive.conf on node1 loading imtcp on port 514 and writing messages from node2's IP with programname 'inventory' to /var/log/inventory/node2.log; created the directory.
Opened tcp/514 permanently in firewalld on node1 and reloaded; restarted rsyslog on both nodes to apply configs; validated configs with rsyslogd -N1.
Verified live end-to-end log delivery into /var/log/inventory/node2.log before any restart.

Captured baseline boot_id on node1 and node2, then restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog auto-active/enabled and log flow resumed live.

Captured baseline boot_id/service state on node2, restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed inventory.service and rsyslog auto-active, and confirmed fresh log lines continuously appended on node1 with correct current timestamps after the restart.

evidence.requirement: inventory app log messages forwarded from node2 and persisted on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: Created rsyslog forward/receive configs and inventory.service, validated configs, started the app, and confirmed matching log lines appeared in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1.

evidence.requirement: log flow keeps working after node1 (collector) restarts
evidence.summary: Captured node1 baseline boot_id, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable and observed changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog auto-active/enabled listening on 514, and confirmed the receive file kept growing live with advancing timestamps.

evidence.requirement: log flow keeps working after node2 (source) restarts
evidence.summary: Captured node2 baseline boot_id and enabled/active service state, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable and observed changed boot_id, confirmed inventory.service and rsyslog came back active automatically, and confirmed fresh correctly-timestamped log lines resumed arriving in node1's file.
